approachQuestion.prompt:
Pair identical labels

A warehouse can bundle two items only when their integer labels match. Return the maximum number of disjoint bundles possible; each item can be used once. Input may be reordered.

Constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200,000; labels are opaque comparison keys; hashing and integer-specific sorting are excluded.

Examples: [4,4,4,7,7,9] → 2. [2,5,8] → 0.

Choose a valid method that meets the full contract with the least unnecessary work.
constraints: The stated input/output and mutation requirements apply to every option.

options.text: Sort labels, count each equal-value run, and add floor(run length / 2).
options.feedback: Within a value group, every two items form one bundle and at most one item remains unused.

options.text: Count distinct labels and divide by two.
options.feedback: There are three distinct labels in [4,4,4,7,7,9], but run lengths 3,2,1 yield two bundles. Distinct-label count does not encode pair multiplicity: [4,4,4] has one distinct label and one bundle, while floor(1/2) is zero.

options.text: Pair each item greedily with the next item in the original input when labels match.
options.feedback: [4,7,4] contains one valid bundle, but the first adjacent check misses it.

options.text: For each item, scan the remaining list for an equal unused label and mark both used.
options.feedback: This correctly constructs disjoint pairs, but repeated full scans cost avoidable work compared with grouping equal labels.

feedback.reason: The three distinct labels in [4,4,4,7,7,9] have run lengths 3,2,1, giving 1+1+0=2 bundles.
details: Comparison-sort the labels, count each maximal equal run, and sum the integer quotient of each run length by two.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed revealed method, choose its tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space bounds. Count copies, sorting buffer and recursion stack; exclude caller input and returned output. Comparison merge sort uses a linear buffer; comparisons and moves are constant-time.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) additional space

feedback.reason: Sorting groups equal labels; the run scan counts disjoint pairs without storing them.
details: Comparison merge sort takes O(n log n) worst-case time; its copied records and merge buffer require O(n) auxiliary space. The recursion stack is O(log n), within O(n). Linear time omits sorting, quadratic time overstates the sort cost; constant space omits the buffer.
